The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
Four people are dead, including three children and one teacher, after a shooting today at
Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, Oregon.
Police say the 16-year-old shooter was found dead inside the school when they arrived.
A community member pursued him into the school and shot him.
Stephen Cook is the superintendent of Bend-Lapine Schools.
We are heartbroken.
We are horrified.
This is the kind of thing you hear about in other places and pray that it never happens
here.
And it has happened here.
Another child and teacher were taken to the hospital.
Nine former FBI employees are suing the bureau and director Kash Patel over what they say
was their unlawful firing after working on an investigation into President Trump.
NPR's Ryan Lucas has more.
The lawsuit says the nine former FBI employees were members of elite counterintelligence and
intelligence squads, and combined they held more than 100 years of experience and service
in the FBI.
They were all assigned to work on the investigation into President Trump's alleged mishandling
of classified documents after his first term in office.
The lawsuit says they were all fired in February, quote, "not for any cause or legitimate reason,
but only to satisfy the president's personal vendetta," end quote.
It says the firings violated their First and Fifth Amendment rights, they are seeking to
be reinstated in their jobs at the FBI, and any back pay they would be due.
Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington.
Ukraine attacked a Russian oil refinery today, abandoning a brief truce involving energy-related
targets that it said Moscow didn't follow.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says he felt betrayed by President Trump after
the U.S. placed restrictions on Starlink systems that Ukraine uses to guide drones.
Trump also recently made a deal to import Russian diesel, despite international efforts
to sanction Russia.
Vice President J.D. Vance stumped for Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers in Michigan today,
calling it the nation's most important race in attacking Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed.
You deserve better than a little weasel who should shut his mouth and show a little gratitude
to the country that gave him everything.
You deserve a senator who is grateful to this country.
President Trump's Iran war and the trade war on Canada are among the top issues in the
Michigan races.
According to the Associated Press, more than 6 million voters have already cast early ballots
for the midterm elections, including roughly 573,000 people in Michigan.
The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration says the U.S. winter will likely be wetter
and warmer this year, but not necessarily snowier due to El Niño.
Meteorologists predict below normal snow in the Northeast, Midwest and Northern Rockies,
but more in the Southeast, West and Southern Rockies.
U.S. stock indexes closed higher today following a shaky day of trading.
The S&P 500 rose more than a quarter of a percent.
This is NPR News.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney says there couldn't be a worse time for Alberta's vote
on a referendum that could set the province on a path toward a future vote on separation
from Canada.
The vote is not a direct referendum on independence.
Carney's remarks come amid President Trump's trade war and repeated threats to make Canada
the 51st state.
France's cybercrime agency is investigating a hacking attack on supermarket refrigeration
systems this week.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports no culprits have yet been named in the hack that has shocked
the country.
Manager of an Intermarché supermarket, Cérie Chibol, got a call about 4 a.m. Monday from
a surveillance company that temperatures were rising in his freezers.
When I opened the freezers, there was no more cold, just hot air coming out.
Even 500 and 700 store refrigeration systems were hacked across France to push the temperatures
from minus 4 degrees Fahrenheit to over 140.
The incident has prompted worries over food security and interference ahead of next spring's
presidential election.
What is weird is that those hackers didn't ask for any money so far.
That's Internet expert Julien Coulombe.
He says the attack could be an attempt to destabilize the companies and the country.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris.
Costco is selling stuffed animals of Jimothy, the short-spined raccoon that became Seattle's
unofficial mascot.
According to the Seattle Times, the plushies are made by dog toy company Think Dog, but
plenty of humans are buying them for themselves for snuggling rather than for chewing.
I'm Rylan Barton, and from Washington, this is NPR.
